entries.reason: The maintainer handle is public by design: package.json carries it in the repository metadata. No other file may name it, not the README, the changelog or the license.

The maintainer's GitHub no-reply identity is the commit identity of the public history, and the tagger of its release tag (design K.5). Only the author, committer and tagger lines are exempt: commit subjects and bodies, and tag names and messages, are scanned like any other text.
Invented token-shaped constant (65 characters; a real fine-grained token has 93) used as a test input, not a credential.
A PEM header line passed as a --private-key flag value to prove that secrets are refused as flags; the body is a placeholder.
A PEM header with a placeholder body, used to test the token-type check; not key material.
A comment that names the PEM header of the key this helper generates at run time; no key material is in the file.
PEM and OpenSSH header lines with placeholder bodies: the inputs of the instruction secret scanner's own test.
A PEM header with a placeholder body in an invented App registration returned by a fake GitHub; not key material.
PEM header line with a placeholder body: an input of the secret-refusal table; not key material.
Invented token-shaped constant (65 characters; a real fine-grained token has 93) passed as a scenario environment value; not a credential.
Two invented token-shaped constants (69 and 71 characters) used to prove that tokens never reach a log or a report; not credentials.
An invented token-shaped constant (71 characters) and a startsWith check on the PEM header of a key generated at run time; not credentials.
Invented token-shaped constants (63 and 65 characters) passed as scenario environment values; not credentials.
